changes.headline: Iran claimed three more tanker mine strikes on Saturday, and the verification layer has not moved
changes.dek: Three tankers claimed mine-struck on Saturday (one eastern strait in the morning, two southern strait in the evening), the second straight day of mine claims, with zero named vessels and zero confirmations. Iran's regular navy said one tanker struck a naval mine in the eastern Strait of Hormuz on Saturday morning, and the IRGC navy said two more tankers, one described as a supertanker, struck mines in the southern strait on Saturday evening while using a prohibited route with tracking systems off. Neither statement names a vessel, a flag, a cargo or a casualty figure. Reuters could not verify the reports, UKMTO had not confirmed them, and no owner, operator, flag state or insurer had confirmed any of the three vessels by Sunday morning. A dismissal attributed to CENTCOM in wire syndication was not matched by a dated Nov 14 CENTCOM release in this check, and the standing US position that the primary transit routes were cleared of mines addresses the primary route rather than the prohibited route the claims describe. The confirmed tempo underneath is separate: at least seven tankers were attacked in the week to Nov 11 on UKMTO's weekly overview, with traffic about 65 percent below pre-war levels.
changes.balance_read: Nothing in the weekend changes a November or December barrel; the claims test is a price test at tonight's reopen, while the basin balance keeps tanking toward December storage of 76.24 million barrels against 80.6 million of working capacity into Tuesday's nominations close.

changes.headline: The Nov 15 Pathways target arrived with no signing announced
changes.dek: The Nov 15 target date has arrived with no signing announced as of Sunday morning; the Oil Sands Growth Program grandfathering line takes effect the same day. Sunday Nov 15 is the target date for binding agreements between Ottawa, Alberta and the five Oil Sands Alliance producers under the July memorandum, and the line after which projects announced under Alberta's Oil Sands Growth Program are grandfathered into that program. As of Sunday morning, no signing, announcement, slip notice or comment dated Nov 14 or 15 was found from either government, the Alliance or any of the five producers, and the Alberta news index carries no release of any kind dated Nov 14 or 15. The Nov 13 program release still quotes Canadian Natural's president as looking forward to finalizing the details of the definitive agreements. The target day is not over, so a later-today announcement remains possible.
changes.balance_read: Silence keeps the growth file conditional for another day while the royalty grandfathering clock runs regardless, against a balance already running about 200 kb/d a month into tanks; a signing later today would move the pipeline file from conditional to committed.

changes.headline: Friday's settles stand: the spread held above $7, December still has not traded, and the confirmed tape is a surplus
changes.dek: Brent to WTI settled above $7 for a second straight session at $7.28; December WCS completed seven sessions without a trade; Brent managed money cut by 111,644 contracts in two weeks. Friday's settles stand with markets closed: Brent Jan27 at $95.84 and WTI Dec26 at $88.56, the spread at $7.28, a second straight settle above $7, and both benchmarks down about 2.5 percent for a second straight week. The confirmed drivers of the two-week decline are the IEA's first surplus print of the war, recovering Gulf exports and Thursday's all-builds US inventory print. December WCS is -$28.27 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 13) on zero lots, a seventh straight session without a trade, while the deferred strip widened on 100 to 845 lots a tenor and the December ARV to TMW spread is +$9.03. Baltic Week 46 fell on every watched route for a second straight week, and Brent managed money stands at +133,813 contracts after two straight large cuts with fresh shorts added.
changes.balance_read: The crude leg stays loose on confirmed data while the product leg stays tight, and the Canadian front month goes into its last full session before nominations still without a trade, with storage heading to 76.24 million barrels in December.

flags.title: December apportionment: the registered call is Light 14 and Heavy 9, nominations close Nov 17
flags.detail: November Mainline apportionment (Light 19 percent at Kerrobert, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert) is in effect. The registered December call is Light 14 percent and Heavy 9 percent. The evidence pack includes the balance build with supply running about 200 kb/d a month above the proven 4,541.6 kb/d egress bound into tanks, a December front month that has not traded in seven sessions, deferred strip widening on volume for two straight sessions, and a Brent to WTI spread at $7.28 with freight falling. December nominations close Tuesday Nov 17; the Enbridge notice follows and grades the call. Trigger: The Enbridge December apportionment notice, or a material change in the physical backdrop before the close

flags.title: The Saturday mine claims get their first price at tonight's reopen, unconfirmed
flags.detail: Iran said three tankers hit naval mines in Hormuz on Saturday, the second straight day of mine claims, with no vessel named and no confirmation from UKMTO, owners or insurers as of Sunday morning. Tonight's futures reopen is the first price on the claims. A move that holds on a confirmed hull is a supply event; a move that fades without confirmation grades the claims as narration priced as fact, against a confirmed surplus backdrop. Trigger: A confirmed hull from an owner, insurer, tracker or UKMTO product, or a reopen move that fades with no confirmation by the London morning

flags.title: Brent positioning has been cut by 111,644 contracts in two weeks, with fresh shorts added
flags.detail: Managed money net long in Brent stands at +133,813 contracts as of Nov 10, the lowest in ten weeks, after cuts of 63,487 and 48,157 in consecutive weeks; the second cut added 16,994 fresh shorts to 137,170 alongside long liquidation. The remaining long-flush risk on a bearish headline is smaller than two weeks ago, and the short base is now large enough to be squeeze fuel under a bullish one. The matching WTI report is delayed to Monday Nov 16. Trigger: The delayed CFTC WTI release on Nov 16, or the next ICE Brent report

forward_calendar.what: Delayed CFTC commitments report for Nov 10 positions
forward_calendar.detail: The federal holiday moved the WTI positioning release to Monday at 3:30 p.m. ET. It is the first snapshot capturing the Nov 4 price collapse, and it lands beside the Brent report's second straight large managed-money cut, to a net long of +133,813 with fresh shorts added. The weekly EIA forecast note for the week ending Nov 13 would also normally be sent Monday.

The deadline for December shipper nominations at 0700 MST. The registered December call (Light 14 percent, Heavy 9 percent) grades against the Enbridge notice that follows, with December still without a trade after seven sessions.

forward_calendar.what: Irving Saint John Operation Osprey resumption date
forward_calendar.detail: The last dated outage in the window is scheduled to resume operations on Nov 18, with no completion release yet.

forward_calendar.what: Athabasca special meeting on the Cenovus arrangement
forward_calendar.detail: Shareholders vote on the plan of arrangement under which Cenovus acquires Athabasca, with proxy and election deadlines on Nov 25 and closing expected in December. Independent proxy advisors including ISS recommend voting for the arrangement.

forward_calendar.what: OPEC+ ministerial meeting on the 2027 framework
forward_calendar.detail: The wider group meets to set the 2027 production framework. The IEA's November report leaves October Gulf exports at 74 percent of pre-war levels and prints Iraq at 4.6 million barrels a day, above its quota.
